reader.summary: South Korea's week was dominated by a sharp escalation in inter-Korean border tensions. Pyongyang threatened to resume propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts across the border, with Kim Yo Jong warning they would be operational within days. Seoul responded by proposing military talks to calm the situation and vowing resolute punishment if North Korea followed through. US and South Korean officials assessed little chance of a Trump-Kim meeting this year. Economically, the chip sector continued to shine: exports for October 1-20 surged 105 percent on record semiconductor sales, and the finance minister projected the chip boom would sustain through 2027. The central bank held rates on October 22 with a hike expected in November. However, the AI trade narrative wobbled as data-center firm Elice plunged roughly 30 percent in its KOSPI debut, and SK Hynix's Solidigm US IPO was placed on hold over dual-listing concerns. A lighter but widely covered story saw a dusky shark nicknamed Bukangi trapped in a canal become a tourist attraction; after two failed rescue attempts, it was finally guided to sea on the third try. Diplomatically, South Korea began withdrawing some embassy staff from Ukraine as the North Korean POW transfer dispute deepened.
